failureMessage: a conflict marker left behind breaks the file, and in a rules or config file it silently changes what the repo instructs every later session and check to do

matchLines.what: a merge-conflict marker line survives here
matchLines.fix: finish the resolution, delete the marker line, then re-read the whole file before staging — never chain the grep that checks for markers with the command that stages

failureMessage: a rule changed one word at a time still shows as a whole-paragraph diff when its bullet is one physical line

maxLineLength.fix: wrap the prose at {bytes} columns — a Markdown bullet continues on an indented line, so the rendering is unchanged

failureMessage: a skill's description is in every session's window whether the skill loads or not, so one written as a summary charges every session for a method almost none of them need

matchLines.fix: cut it to what decides whether to reach for the skill, and leave the method to the body, which loads only when the skill does

failureMessage: without merge=ours a conflicting merge on a generated file gets hand-resolved and desyncs from its source

requireIndexCoverage.what: a GENERATED file with no merge=ours .gitattributes entry
requireIndexCoverage.fix: add `{base} merge=ours` to .gitattributes so a conflicting merge auto-resolves — the session-start hook already sets the `merge.ours.driver` config in the clone

requireIndexCoverage.what: a GENERATED file under .claudinite/ that .claudinite/.gitattributes does not cover
requireIndexCoverage.fix: the engine converges that file — run `node .claudinite/shared/engine/converge-wiring.mjs <owner/repo>` (silent until an engine that writes it has arrived)

failureMessage: a hand-maintained catalog that omits a real pack misroutes readers and hides capability; the check keeps the index honest against the tree

requireIndexCoverage.what: the pack "{name}" exists on disk but is not listed in packs/README.md
requireIndexCoverage.fix: add a "{name}" entry to packs/README.md (or delete the pack if it is dead)

failureMessage: a suite driven by git ls-files never executes an untracked test, so a green run is not coverage of it

flagUntrackedFilesMatching.what: {path} is untracked, so the suite you are certifying never ran it
flagUntrackedFilesMatching.fix: git add {path}, then re-run the suite

failureMessage: under the default files_with_matches mode a context flag is silently ignored, so the call answers a file list and never the lines it asked for

guardToolCalls.what: a Grep with a context flag and no output_mode: "content"
guardToolCalls.fix: add output_mode: "content" to the same call

failureMessage: a GENERATED file is written by its generator, and a hand edit is overwritten by the next run while its merge conflicts are resolved by neither side

guardToolCalls.what: a hand edit of a GENERATED file
guardToolCalls.fix: change the generator (or its inputs) and re-run it

failureMessage: the harness rejects a wake-up that carries no prompt, and a rejection leaves no fallback armed

guardToolCalls.what: a ScheduleWakeup call without a prompt
guardToolCalls.fix: pass prompt — the instruction the woken turn acts on — on every call that is not stop: true

failureMessage: a trailing tail or head replaces the pipeline's exit code with its own and discards the earlier lines a failure would have shown

guardToolCalls.what: a run whose output ends in "{match}"
guardToolCalls.fix: redirect the run to a file, read $? from that invocation, and grep the file for the slice you need

failureMessage: pkill -f matches the invoking shell's own command line, which carries the pattern

guardToolCalls.fix: bracket one character of the pattern ([h]ttp.server) and never chain the pkill

failureMessage: an unnarrowed list or search answers with a single-line dump that Read cannot slice

guardToolCalls.fix: pass fields (and perPage) naming just what the next step reads

failureMessage: a blocking question spends real human wall-clock, and most are already answered by an instruction in context, by state one read away, or by the recommended option being the status quo

guardToolCalls.what: a blocking question to the owner
guardToolCalls.fix: ask only a fork you cannot resolve yourself and batch every open decision into this one call; for anything answerable from the instruction or the tree, act and say what you assumed

failureMessage: each Bash call is a fresh shell, so a wait with no job launched in the same call returns at once, looking like a satisfied wait

guardToolCalls.what: a "{wait}" in a shell that launched nothing
guardToolCalls.fix: consume the launching call's own result, or run the command with run_in_background: true and act on its notification

failureMessage: a call made only to occupy the turn can come back with no visible text, which the harness then interrupts to ask for a real response

guardToolCalls.what: a no-op call ("{field}") made only to pass the turn
guardToolCalls.fix: say in plain text that you are waiting, with no tool call

failureMessage: a child issue linked only by a number in its body leaves the parent blind to what is still open under it

guardToolCalls.what: an issue filed under another ("{match}") with no parent_issue_number
guardToolCalls.fix: pass parent_issue_number on the create, or attach it afterwards with sub_issue_write (method add, sub_issue_id the id the create returned, not its number)
